title: Memory and speed: dtypes, chunks, and when pandas is the wrong tool

videos.script: Someone sends you a file of five gigabytes. Your laptop has eight. Will it load? {{file}} The answer depends less on the rows than on their types. {{types}} Read as text, the trips take more memory than the file takes on disk. Typed, they take a fifth of that. {{fifth}} This lesson measures where the memory goes, and gets it back. {{measure}} Read fewer columns. Give them their types as you read. Store in Parquet what you will read again. {{steps}} And when the file is larger than memory, read it in pieces. That works for counts and sums, and quietly fails for a median. {{chunks}} Past that, pandas is the wrong tool, and the lesson ends by naming the right ones. {{end}}
